review_type: source-grounded AI review; not physician adjudication
reviewed_components: all clinical facts and measured quantities
corrections: Text-flag versus Table 1 value pairs (10 labs plus Case 1 heart rate and Case 5 normal vital signs) un-quarantined: the text fact keeps the source's own flag (text_value now the source word instead of "... per case text"), the Table 1 value fact is included without a flag, and each pair keeps one ambiguity stating that the value lies outside the printed interval, must_not_infer the flag from the range (OBS-FLAG; orchestrator ruling)

p1: TED severity moderate-to-severe (text) vs moderate (Table 1) adjudicated as compatible wording, not a conflict: f045 and f046 included with an ambiguity; the severity-less duplicate f044 (same quote as f045) removed and its references repointed to f045

Cases 1 and 5: 3-month (text) vs 4-month (Table 1) follow-up statements adjudicated as not a conflict (findings agree; the source never identifies them as the same assessment and reports follow-up beyond 3 months): p1-f058/f059 and p5-f060/f062/f064/f065 included with their own literal times and an ambiguity forbidding a merge; new event p1-e06 for the 4-month Table 1 statement
p3-f022 hypertension: temporality historical -> unknown and role history -> comorbidity (the sentence says "controlled hypertension", not "history of"; TEMPORALITY)

p4: Case 4 inflammatory-marker conflict narrowed to its attribute: f043 (CRP slightly elevated, text) and f044 (now "Inflammatory markers" normal, Table 1) stay review-only source_conflict; ESR "remained unchanged" (f042) included (no classification); the thyroid-function clause of the Table 1 cell split out as new included fact p4-f050
p5-f054 oral analgesics every 6 h for one month promoted to included: the frequency/duration applies to the analgesics under both readings; only the corticosteroid scope stays an ambiguity

Table 2 rows checked: they label patients by number in a "Patients" column (1, 2, 5 / 3, 4), not by "Case N"; the assignment patient N = Case N is kept (numbering and treatments match the case reports) and recorded as one ambiguity per patient

Timeline: new events p1-e06 (asymptomatic at 4 months, Table 1), p1-e07 and p2-e08 (two previous AstraZeneca doses), p1-e08 (tapering of oral corticosteroids initiated), p4-e06 (selenium and levothyroxine continued due to persistent exophthalmos); 17 relations added (8 -> 25), each with a literal order quote: "previously received" before the third dose, cohort sentence "TED occurred between 3 and 20 days after receiving a COVID-19 vaccine" (explicitly all five patients) for vaccine -> TED diagnosis, Figure 1 caption "3-month follow-up after treatment" for treatment -> 3-month follow-up in every case, "Subsequently" (p2), "continued" (p3, p4), "Initially" (p5 tonsillitis -> TED diagnosis and later management), 3-month -> 1-year follow-up (p5)
p1 and p2 outcome summary claims reworded so the 3-month time is not attached to untimed laboratory and treatment sentences
unresolved: Table 1 values are recorded without a time because its caption mixes baseline and outcome characteristics; times are kept only where a cell or sentence states them.

Where the case text classifies a result (normal, elevated, low) and the Table 1 value lies outside its printed reference interval, the text flag and the table value are separate included facts, the table value carries no flag, and an ambiguity records the discrepancy; flags are never derived from intervals.

Source conflicts (review-only, conflicting attribute only): Case 3 exophthalmos laterality at presentation (bilateral vs unilateral left), TED severity (moderate-to-severe vs mild) and 3-month thyroid function (free T4 slightly below normal vs thyroid function normalized); Case 4 inflammatory markers at follow-up (CRP slightly elevated vs normal). Case 1 severity (moderate-to-severe vs moderate) and the 3-month vs 4-month follow-up statements of Cases 1 and 5 are recorded as ambiguities, not conflicts.

Table 1 names products (ChAdOx1 nCoV-19, prednisone, methylprednisolone) that differ from the text wording (AstraZeneca vaccine, oral corticosteroids, corticosteroids); equivalence is not asserted except for the case 2 intravenous corticosteroid regimen, whose doses are identical.
Statements that vaccination history was obtained from the patient and confirmed from medical records have no clinical section and are not recorded as facts.

Discussion, limitations and conclusion paragraphs describe the series; counts such as numbers of patients with a finding were not copied to individuals. Figure 1 shows photographs with black rectangles over the eyes; the caption-level statement of improvement is not recorded as an individual fact.
The retrospective CAS estimates and the Table 2 group outcomes are assigned to the patients whose numbers the source lists, taking patient N as Case N (recorded as an ambiguity per patient).

key_findings: Five-woman case series; roster order and the Case 1-5 narratives, every Table 1 column and the Figure 1 rows matched one to one.

Twelve text-classification versus Table 1 value pairs (10 labs, Case 1 heart rate, Case 5 normal vital signs) are not conflicts: the text flag and the unflagged table value are both included with an ambiguity each.

Genuine conflicts kept review-only on the conflicting attribute only: Case 3 exophthalmos laterality, Case 3 TED severity (moderate-to-severe vs mild), Case 3 free T4 slightly below normal vs thyroid function normalized at 3 months, Case 4 CRP slightly elevated vs inflammatory markers normal.
Case 1 severity (moderate-to-severe vs moderate) and the 3-month vs 4-month follow-up statements of Cases 1 and 5 are compatible statements recorded as ambiguities.
Included facts whose quotes carry quarantined words (p3 f030 exophthalmos, p3 f033 TED) leave the quarantined attribute out of their fields.
Table 2 labels patients by number, not by Case; patient N = Case N kept with an ambiguity per patient.
Relations raised from 8 to 25 with literal order evidence (previously, the cohort onset sentence, the Figure 1 caption "follow-up after treatment", Subsequently, continued, Initially).
Figure 1 viewed at full resolution and 2x/4x crops: ten eye-region photographs with black rectangles, Case 1-5 headings printed; visual, figure-EHR and privacy sidecars agree with the pixels.
residual_risks: Whether the 3-month and 4-month follow-up statements of Cases 1 and 5 describe one visit is not stated; both are included with their own times.
Product names in Table 1 (ChAdOx1 nCoV-19, prednisone) are not merged with the text wording (AstraZeneca vaccine, oral corticosteroids) because the source never equates them.
Table 1 cells are recorded without times except where a cell states one; row labels such as "at presentation" are not used as times.
The Case 5 corticosteroid frequency/duration scope remains an ambiguity.
